steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Didn't the Signori dei Lupi agree not to meddle in the affairs of mortals?

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: I changed my mind. Bernardo ruined my plans!

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: I spent sixty-eight years grooming him.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: And now he's killed himself just to deny my victory!

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Wh-What did you say?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: My father... killed himself?
His father's interpretation of the Signori dei Lupi and the game flash through Leontuzzo's mind.
He suddenly understands that the words his father spoke to him in the church were a kind of approval for him...
And his last words.
His father had planned to take his own life all along.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: The price for insulting the Signori dei Lupi is a heavy one.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: He may dead, but I won't stop until his bloodline is ended.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Son of Bernardo, you will pay for the sins of your father!

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: The price is his bloodline and your life!

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Price?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Did you say 'price?'

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: My father may have been wrong, but his dream was always about bringing change to the times.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: He wanted a Siracusa without the famiglie, and spent his entire life planning it.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I thought his own family was a chip to him.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I thought he acted when he did because it was the right time.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But now I know.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: He decided he was out of time. This was his only chance to get revenge on you and achieve his dream.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: I taught him everything he knew! He repaid me with betrayal!

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You wouldn't understand.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Signore dei Lupi on high, thinking everything under his control.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: To father, even his own life was just another chip.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: He was determined to make his dream come true, even if it meant paying the ultimate price.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But you're the one who will pay!

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Ignorant whelp!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Welcome back, Texas!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Are you done over there?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Time to clean up the trouble over here.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: The last Texas.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Do not forget who permitted you to break from Siracusa.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: How dare you defy me?!

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I kept my bargain with Bernardo. I owe you nothing.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Fool!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Bernardo killed himself?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: The game is over, Lavinia.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: So that's what you really meant...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: A Siracusa without the famiglie. That was your true dream.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Why didn't you tell me?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Try to keep your head in the fight, Judgie.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Lappland—

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Why didn't you tell me you were throwing a party, Texas?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: You would've come anyway.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Yeah, you're right.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Get lost, cub without a pack. There's no place for you here.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Let me tell you some good news, Signore dei Lupi, Figlio dei Lupi, whatever you are.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Starting now, everything Siracusan is my enemy.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Even supernatural beings like you.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Idiot!

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: What about you, boss? If you were there, looking me in the eye, would you tell me without a doubt, that you choose your dreams, like Leon?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I mean... I don't know the answer anymore.

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: Stay focused, if you don't want to die.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You're—

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: The feeble Fang of Agnese.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Did you think yourself worthy to stand before me just because you caught a glimpse of the death of my Fang?

steps.name: Lunacub
steps.text: I promised Bernardo that I'd help his kin.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Agnese has raised a feeble Fang.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: It's time to put an end to her part in this game.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: You cannot destroy me, no matter what you do.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: You cannot even harm me.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Humans built cities, trapped themselves within, and think themselves the masters of the lands beneath them.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Do not presume to have risen because you learned to use a few tools.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: You have never conquered the wastes.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Ladies and gentleman.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: You stand in the presence of the Emperor, Lungmen's superstar!

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Boss?!

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Lemme take this chance to remind you your vacation's almost up, Texas.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Why are you here?

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: You askin' me?

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Sora and the girls ran off after you.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: You know what the past month's been like for me?

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: I ain't been this bored in three thousand years!

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: I got nobody to party with!

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Emperor—

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Hold it, Zaaro.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: You gonna say I got no business in Siracusa. It ain't my right to stick my flipper in here.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Honestly, I don't give a shit.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: But, if I think on it, I'm gonna pass on some dumbass fight with you...

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Beatin' you at your own game, that'd make me happier.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: So—
Shadow after shadow emerges from beneath Emperor's feet and takes corporeal form.
Zaaro knows them, of course. They are the Signori dei Lupi who have lost in this round.
They are here for one reason.
He broke the rules.
They can accept how he played, but they will not permit the rules to be broken.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Look, I brought the other Wolf Lords. They bored too.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Lemme give you the good news.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: You're a loser.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: In pretty much every way a man can be a loser.
The Signori dei Lupi are immortal, but over the long years, they have long learned how to contain, suppress, even torment each other.
Against so many beings of his kind, Zaaro knows that resistance is futile.
After a moment of silence, he lowers his proud head.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Tell ya the truth, Zaaro?

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Your whole thing, the way you talk about power, the way you play with it, gives me the heebie-jeebies.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: The way you stew in your anger, lookin' to tear everything in your way to pieces...

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: That's what shows you still true to your nature.

spans.text: what shows you still true to your nature.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: But all you wolves, don't you get bored playin' a dumbass game like this for thousands of years?

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: You oughta come to Lungmen. I'll teach ya to play poker.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Or mahjong. Mahjong ain't bad.
Zaaro ignores Emperor's jabs.
He takes one last, long look at Leontuzzo, then his silhouette becomes less and less distinct, until he fades away completely in the wind.
It is as though he never existed.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Thanks, Boss.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Don't thank me.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Someone woulda done somethin', even if it wasn't me.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: She just delegated the job. Didn't ya, sexy?

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: It's been a long time since anyone called me 'sexy.'

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: You're welcome to spend some time enjoying Siracusa, if you like.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Just call me Emperor.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Interesting name. You're not arrogant or ignorant, like the Signori dei Lupi, Siracusa welcomes you, Emperor.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: I think Siracusa's gonna like me.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Signora Sicilia!

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: The games of the Signori dei Lupi are archaic and stupid.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Leontuzzo, son of Bernardo.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Rest assured, he'll never trouble you again.
Leontuzzo cannot move an inch.
He realizes that everything ended the moment the old woman appeared.
Not just the game of the Signori dei Lupi, but their resistance as well.
The old woman before him looks kind and cordial, but he knows that he will die in the most painful way possible, if he makes one wrong move.
He also knows, however, that to back down now is to see all his effort, all that he believes in, fade into dream.
He looks over at Lavinia and sees the same thought in her eyes.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Pardon me, Signora Sicilia. I didn't expect to have the honor of your presence in this way.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You may already know what happened. You may already have made your decision.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But I hope you'll give me and Lavinia a chance.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: A chance. What kind of chance?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: A chance to talk.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Even if we're doomed to die, I hope you'll grant us an audience before that happens.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Ah.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Agenir always says I should listen to the youths more.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: I think he overestimates his age.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Come with me, children. You have earned the chance.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: May I have a moment first?

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I would like to take one last look at Bernardo.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Exusiai! Texas!

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: You okay?!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: We're fine.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: ...Yeah.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: What are you doing here?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: I was too worried. Giovanna's stable now, so I brought Croissant.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Looks like everything's more-or-less hunky-dory over here, though?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I guess so.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Whew... it still feels like something's missing, but I guess we can throw our party now?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: You guys decide what kind of party you want.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Where are you going, Texas?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Toilet.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Toilet isn't that way.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Feel a weight off your shoulders? Like you just got over a hill?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: There's still big trouble waiting, right there.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Ha. Shall we go?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: We'll go.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: By the way, Texas.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I got a letter from Signora Sicilia before you went back to Siracusa.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Cool.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Guess what it said?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: No thanks.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Oh, you're no fun. Signora Sicilia invited me to join the Bocca al Lupo.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Bocca al Lupo...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Basically, become one of her wolves.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: So I burned the letter.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I figured I was gonna get some Siracusans giving me trouble for a while.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Then you went back to Siracusa, all of a sudden.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Do you have any idea how surprised I was when I realized you were gone?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: So you've made up your mind?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I'll stay and help Lavinia and Leontuzzo.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I've made up my mind too.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I heard you made a hell of a scene with your own famiglia.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I just went to say goodbye to my father.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Texas... Do you really not get what I see in you?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Sometimes I think I do.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Sometimes I think I don't.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: All I know is that you seem to have gotten over something.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Oh? Are you showing concern for me?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I just think you're kind of annoying.
The pair were walking side-by-side, but now they head to opposite ends of the clearing, as if by some silent agreement.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: At the end of the day, we have to do this.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I guess so.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Do you remember?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Seven years ago, you came to me, in front of the burning mansion, looking to get away from it all.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I got hell for it that day.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Seven years later, you came to me again, in a rainy park, to issue a silly challenge to Siracusa.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I'll kill you today.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: That's my line.
The sound of weapons clashing fills the park.
No tricks, no fooling around. Every attack is intended to kill.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You could call me your past, Texas.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I believed that no one could escape this swamp.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You escaped your past, once, and made up your mind to cut all ties with it, after returning to Siracusa.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You proved to everyone that you had what it took to escape the swamp.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You're staying here of your own accord, to help that young cub change the place.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: You're giving me too much credit.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: My dream has always been to live a simple life with a few good friends.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I'll defend it, if someone threatens to destroy it.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: There's nothing complicated about it.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: I never truly knew you, Cellinia.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: I didn't realize how Siracusa exhausted you, or how you resented Columbia.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: Now that I think about it, I was like my grandma.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: She spent her entire life hoping that old Salvadore would change his mind.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: But she never even asked, never tried to fight for it.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: The same for me. I assumed the good times would last forever.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: I was so proud, and arrogant.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: You wouldn't mind me staying with you, and I would love to chat more with Sora.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: But I don't deserve that. Not yet.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: And so, let me close the curtains on Act 3 of La Morte di Texas, on Cellinia Texas's story.

spans.text: And so, let me close the curtains on Act 3 of

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: You're free, Cellinia.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: No one defines you.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: So let me put it a different way.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You're my nightmare, Texas.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You always surprise me.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You're always a step ahead of me.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You made all the decisions that I couldn't.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: And now I can finally say this, after finally taking that step, like you did.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You're right.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: There's nothing complicated about it.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: If I hated everything about Siracusa so much, I should've destroyed it.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: In the end, you're the one who made me take this step.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: That's why you said goodbye to your father, and why you're standing here in front of me.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: You want to settle things with your past.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Yes. Just like you.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: We didn't have to go at each other's throats like this.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: But it happened.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: We each decided, on our own, that to kill each other is the way to settle things.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: The best way to say our goodbyes.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: The one who survives will become stronger.
Not that Lappland has become stronger than Texas, or that Texas has become weak.
Just like how Lappland did not lose to Texas seven years ago because she was weaker.
They were evenly matched from the beginning.
What determines the outcome is Lady Luck, perhaps... or more importantly, strength of will.
Seven years ago, Lappland lost the battle of wills.
But now, having said goodbye to the famiglia, her will is no weaker than Texas's.
Either may win, and either may lose.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: It's over.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Texas!

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Stay back.
Texas takes one look at Sora, then closes her eyes.
Lappland thought she knew Texas well enough.
What did she not know?
She bore witness to Texas's exhaustion with Siracusa, and her decision to declare war on the country.
Texas's decisions surprised her each time.
But this time, she thought, it would not be so.
One lives, the other dies. There would be no other end.
But as she saw the unwillingness to let go in Texas's eyes, she once again realized that she was wrong.
At the very end, in the ending that Lappland wrote for herself, Texas has surprised her, once again.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Ha. Alright.
Lappland sees this battle as a farewell, a liberation.
Lose, and she will accept her death.
Win, and she will be able to let it all go.
When the pin by the name of Texas is pulled from her consciousness, a lunatic by the name of Lappland would be born.
But it never happened.
Because—

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Texas. So you were just Texas after all.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Of course I'm just Texas.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Looks like I'm just Lappland.
Lappland extends a hand to Texas.
Texas takes the hand.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Texas, am I your friend, or your enemy?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: You're my friend, and my enemy.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Then go.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Let me do what a friend should.
Texas nods to the others, and walks towards Grey Hall.
It is all so natural, as though it was always the way things should be.
When Lavinia walks into the church and sees the body sitting silently on the pew, she finally accepts the truth—
Bernardo is dead.
She sits by the man who was both father and brother, the man who had such an impact on her life, and stays silent.
In the end, she says nothing.
But she holds Bernardo's lifeless hand, as though communicating something, or getting something from him.
Then, she turns and leaves.
The dead are dead and gone. She must move on.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: I heard my friends talking about what you did.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Let me ask you one thing, child.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: All the nations across these lands are seeking change, trying to move with the times.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: But the impetus for change is an awareness of inadequacy, or a search for breakthrough.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Does Siracusa need that? Does Siracusa really need to change?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Do you think... that the famiglia is something that must exist?

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Nothing is. But it existed for centuries before I was born.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: We can't deny our history, or so easily destroy what already exists, can we?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: That's why you chose to continue the famiglia system when you established Grey Hall, except now all the famiglie have to operate under your control.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I don't intend to deny it.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: In fact, I think it was the correct decision, in its time.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: But things are different now?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The return of the Columbian famiglie brought advanced technology and philosophy.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The Columbians are exerting an increasing influence on famiglia-style rule, but many haven't realized it.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Some of what my father did was overly radical.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Our motivations are different, and so are our means.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But one thing is the same.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: We both believe that—

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Siracusa doesn't need the famiglie anymore.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: What are you planning to do, then?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The simplest thing would be to kill you here, or die trying.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But that's the choice my father would have made.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: As for me...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I would like to borrow a city.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: An interesting proposal.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: A new city needs new blood.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: But you're on your own, child.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: How am I supposed to believe that you can reach your goal?
The doors of Grey Hall are pushed open, before Signora Sicilia finished her sentence.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Cellinia. The last Texas.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Come here and let me get a good look at you.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: I see your grandfather in you.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: ...Thank you.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Looks like Giovanna has given you the necklace that I gave her.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: What is it you want?

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: If you want to go back to Lungmen, I guarantee that Siracusa will never disturb you again.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I want to ask you to spare Famiglia Rossati.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Oh? That's a surprise.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Wallach assassinated Giovanna, and tried to kill you many times.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Do you really want to spare him?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: They're only trying to survive, in their own way.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: You can keep the necklace. I never intended to do anything to them.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Or, you can trade it for the right to leave Siracusa forever.
Texas sits down by Leontuzzo's side.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Don't need that. I'm extending my vacation.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: What about you, Lappland?

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Lone wolf, Saluzzo's traitor.
Lappland walks to Texas's side with a jesting smirk on her face.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Heh. I got a simple dream.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I wanna destroy Siracusa, just like them.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: The difference is that I'm not as civilized.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: And you, Judge Lavinia, instrument of my will?
Lavinia stands behind Leontuzzo.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Your will was once Siracusa itself.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But now, I'm going to change it.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: You believe that I'm wrong?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I believe that no one can be right forever.
Signora Sicilia casts her gaze at the four young people before her.
One who came from the strongest famiglia in Siracusa, whose upbringing made him long for a civilized future. Denied by his position, he chose to bury his head in the sand.
One who came from modest beginnings, who earned the favor of the famiglie. It filled her with doubt about herself, and so she chose to deceive herself.
One who came from the oldest famiglia in Siracusa, who hated everything that it asked of her. It drove her to rebellion, down a path of madness.
One who came from the strongest famiglia in Columbia, who became exhausted with the existence of the famiglia itself. She chose to run away in silence.
They want to change Siracusa for different reasons, but they all came together, in the end.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: I won't live forever, but I have a few decades left.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Until the moment that my eyes close forever, Siracusa will continue to enjoy the peace that I bring.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: What about you, child?

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: You stand on your father's shoulders, seeking to make the system better and fairer.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Do you think you chose the correct path?

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: If I gave you Siracusa, could you guarantee that she would walk a better path, and become a better country?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: ...I can't guarantee that.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But, just as you're willing to listen to me here today...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: If someone else comes along, looking to change my ways...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I'm willing to sit down and hear him out.
Signora Sicilia smiles.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: You see, I don't hear any fighting. They're fine.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: You're the only one who could be so at ease like this. That's the head of state there, you know?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Sorry for making you worry.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: It's fine.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Huh? Where's Lappland?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: She...
Texas casts her gaze in a certain direction.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: She's fulfilled her duty as a friend. Who knows what form she'll take, when she shows herself next time?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: The only thing I can be sure is this.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: We haven't seen the last of her.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: My head hurts just thinkin' about it.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Never mind. Let's see how Giovanna's doing.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Giovanna, we're back!
The room is empty.
Sora's joy quickly turns to confusion.
Then, she sees a stack of paper on the desk.
It is a script.
Sora flips over the first page.
'Dedicated to my dear old friend, Cellinia.
And my new friends, Penguin Logistics.'

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: The part that Giovanna was struggling with in Act 3 of La Morte di Texas...

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Is this what you left for us?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: You didn't have to leave.
